title: SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira
body:
For everyone who plans or reports work in Jira. This is the home of the SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira documentation. Learn what the app does, who it is for and where to start.

SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira: rank your projects, see where capacity runs out, plan the week and report with numbers you can check.

Portfolio, capacity and the weekly plan in one place, live from Jira

Many teams keep a portfolio spreadsheet next to Jira, and it is out of date within days. SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira reads your projects, estimates, worklogs, teams and dates live from Jira, as the person who is signed in. You rank your projects once. The cockpit hands out your teams' capacity from the top of the ranking down, support first. The waterline shows where capacity runs out this quarter. Team leads plan the week on a board and write the plan to Jira when they are ready. Management gets a one-page report. Hover any number to see how it was calculated, and undo any change you make.

How it works

From setup to everyday use in four steps.

📊 See what fits this quarter

The portfolio in rank order with the orange waterline.

All projects in one ranked list with progress, forecast, maturity and health. Drag a project up or down and the waterline moves at once. Projects above it can be fully staffed; below it, you see the missing hours per team.

🗓️ Plan the week, then write it to Jira

Weekly planning: people and weeks, with absences, holidays and free time.

A person × week board for your weekly meeting. Drag work to another week or person, let Optimize suggest how to finish sooner or smooth overload. Nothing reaches Jira until you click Apply in Jira.

📄 Report with numbers you can defend

The C-level report: the situation on one page.

Key figures, who waits for whom and capacity by rank per quarter, as PDF or Excel. Lotse, the cockpit's built-in navigator, answers questions from your data and names the source of every number. It works without AI.

 #F4F5F7:bust_in_silhouette:

For everyone

  • See your tasks of the week under My work.
  • Book your hours in one grid, straight into Jira.
  • Fill in missing values on your own work items.

Start with the User guide.

 #FFF4EE:busts_in_silhouette:

For project admins and management

  • Rank projects and watch the waterline.
  • Maintain team capacities and plan the week.
  • Compare plan and actual, dispatch support tickets.
  • Share the C-level report.

Start with the User guide.

 #EAF2FF:gear:

For Jira admins

  • Set the cockpit up in 6 steps; most of it is detected for you.
  • Decide who sees what, including people's individual values.
  • Decide whether AI is allowed. It is off by default.
  • See every change in the audit log.

Start with Getting started.

Explore the documentation

title: Portfolio Cockpit – Getting started
body:
For Jira admins. You will install SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira, understand what Jira asks you to approve, and finish the 6-step setup so your teams can start.

 2

Before you start

  • You need a Jira Cloud site and the Administer Jira permission (you are a Jira admin).
  • Plan about 10 minutes. Most settings are detected for you.
  • Any Jira edition works when each Jira space is one project in your portfolio. If your projects are work items (for example an issue type "Project") in a Plans hierarchy, Jira Premium is recommended.
  • Optional: Jira Service Management, if you want the support area with SLAs.
  • Optional: an organization admin of your Atlassian organization, to allow the app to read Atlassian Teams (see below).

Step 1: Install the app

SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira will be available on the Atlassian Marketplace.

  1. In Jira, open Settings (⚙️) → Apps.
  2. Search the Marketplace for SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira and click the app.
  3. Review the permissions Jira shows you (see below) and confirm.

Until the Marketplace listing is public, SUPERPORT sends your Jira admin an installation link instead. Open it, choose your site and confirm the permissions.

What Jira asks you to approve, and why

During installation Jira lists the permissions the app needs. In plain words:

PermissionWhat the app does with it
Read Jira workRead projects, work items, estimates, worklogs, dates, links, versions and service queues to work out the portfolio, capacity, plans and reports. Always as the person who is signed in, so everyone sees only what Jira lets them see.
Write Jira workOnly when someone clicks: book worklogs under My work, apply the weekly plan (dates, assignee), fill missing values, set the app's own fields and link support tickets. Each change can be undone.
Read user informationCheck the signed-in person's permissions and groups (for the cockpit's roles), and show the names of assignees and worklog authors.
Store app dataKeep the app's own data in Atlassian's storage for Forge apps: configuration, ranking, health, capacities, plan snapshots, audit log and personal preferences.
Send Jira notificationsOptional reminders and booking notices. Nothing is sent until a Jira admin switches them on.
Read Confluence spaces, write Confluence pagesPublish the C-level report as a Confluence page, only on someone's click and only into approved spaces. Off by default; see the Admin guide.
Read teams and users (Teamwork Graph)Read your Atlassian Teams and their members, as the signed-in person, so capacity can be planned per team. An organization admin grants this. Without it the app still works, and you maintain team members in the cockpit instead.
Forge LLM (AI)Optional AI features run on Atlassian's own AI service inside Atlassian's cloud. Nothing is sent to it until a Jira admin switches AI on.

The app never asks for a password or an API token, and it connects to no servers outside Atlassian. Details are on Security & privacy.

What the app adds to Jira

  • Three app fields: Portfolio Rank (read-only on Jira screens, usable in JQL), T-Shirt Size and Target Quarters.
  • A panel Planning check on each work item.
  • A workflow validator Original Estimate required (Portfolio Cockpit). It does nothing until you add it to a workflow transition.
  • A page in each project, a page in the Jira Apps menu and an admin page.

Step 2: Open the app

Open Apps → SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit. Before the setup is done, you see Almost there – the cockpit is not set up yet. Click Set up now. Everyone else sees Ask your Jira admin to set up Portfolio Cockpit. until you save the setup.

You can also reach the same configuration from Jira settings (⚙️) → Apps → Portfolio Cockpit.

Step 3: Set up in 6 steps

The configuration opens with Welcome! We detected your Jira structure. and a short guide Set up in 6 steps. Check each suggestion; nothing is assumed. Leave empty what you do not have.

  1. Hierarchy & projects. What is a project? Choose Projects are spaces (every Jira space is a project, any edition) or Projects are work items (an issue type such as "Project" in the Plans hierarchy). Then switch on the levels below. Exactly one level must be Estimation & time tracking.
  2. Fields & required fields. Map team, start date and owner. Leave empty what you do not have.
  3. Teams. Check that it says Connected and choose which teams appear in the cockpit (for example Only teams with tasks).
  4. Roles and permissions. Map Jira groups to Project admin and Management. Without a mapping, only Jira admins see the report and individual values.
  5. Locations and holidays. Create your locations, each with a holiday calendar and working days.
  6. Support & SLAs (optional). Choose service spaces, software or business spaces, or queues for support work.

Click Save. You see Configuration saved – effective immediately, and the cockpit is now available to everyone.

Team members come from Atlassian Teams. Who belongs to which team is maintained in Atlassian Teams (home.atlassian.com → Teams). The cockpit syncs every 5 minutes, or at once with Sync now. In the cockpit you only maintain hours, location and shares.

Step 4: Build the portfolio

  1. Open the Portfolio tab.
  2. Click Add project and add your projects.
  3. Drag them into one unique ranking, most important first. You can also use Alt + ↑/↓.

The portfolio in rank order. The orange waterline shows how far this quarter's capacity reaches.

Step 5: Enter capacities

  1. Open Teams and pick a team.
  2. Open Maintain capacities.
  3. Enter each person's weekly hours, daily business and location. For people in several teams, set their team shares in %.

People without their own values show Default values – not maintained yet until someone enters their hours. You or your project admins can do this step later; the waterline improves as capacities are filled in.

Where to find the app in Jira

WhereWhat
Apps → SUPERPORT Portfolio CockpitThe full cockpit. The tabs you see depend on your role.
A project's navigation → Portfolio CockpitThe cockpit, opened on that project.
A work item → Planning checkTeam, assignee load, conflicts and dependencies for this work item.
Jira settings (⚙️) → Apps → Portfolio CockpitThe configuration, for Jira admins.

You're done when…

#E9F7EF:white_check_mark:
  • The Portfolio tab shows your projects in rank order with numbers. Where estimates are missing, it says so plainly, for example No original estimate yet.
  • Configuration → Teams says Connected with the number of teams.
  • Configuration → Audit log lists your setup.
  • A colleague in a mapped group opens the app and sees the tabs of their role. Everyone else sees My work.
  • The Planning check panel opens on a work item.

The first time someone opens the cockpit, a short tour shows them around. They can start it again with ? at the top right.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Portfolio Cockpit – User guide
body:
For everyone who uses the cockpit: team members, project admins and management. You will learn the everyday tasks, from booking your week to ranking projects, planning the week and sharing the C-level report.

 2

Find your way around

Open Apps → SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit. Your role decides which tabs you see. Hover a tab to see what it is for. A number on a tab means something there needs you.

TabWhat it is forWho sees it (default)
My workYour tasks of the week. Book hours and fill in missing values.Everyone
PortfolioAll projects in rank order with progress, health, who waits for whom and the waterline.Project admins, management
ProjectsOne project in detail: action needed, missing values, structure and capacity.Project admins, management
TeamsOne team: what it works on, how loaded it is, and its capacities.Project admins, management
Weekly planningWho works on what and when. Move tasks and apply them in Jira.Project admins, management
Plan vs. actualWhere the hours went, compared with the week's plan, and whether everyone booked enough.Project admins, management
SupportDispatch tickets, SLAs and the support reserve. Only shown when support is set up.Project admins, management
C-level reportThe situation on one page, as PDF or Excel.Management
ConfigurationAll settings.Jira admins

At the top you also find:

  • Search or jump … (Ctrl K): find projects, work items, views and actions, or hand Lotse a question.
  • Ask and Lotse: ask questions in your own words (see below).
  • ↶ with a number: what you can undo. Ctrl/⌘ + Z undoes your last action.
  • DE | EN: switch the language. ? restarts the tour.

Every number explains itself. Hover it to see the calculation. In the Ctrl K search, Proof – check the numbers against Jira lists the work items behind a figure.

Book your week

Under My work you see your own week: your team, weekly hours, the next absence and public holiday, and your tasks.

  1. Open My work. Use Previous week, This week and Next week to switch weeks.
  2. Type hours into the cell of a task and day, for example 1.5 or 1:30.
  3. Press Enter. The hours are booked in Jira as a worklog, with your own Jira permissions. An empty cell removes the booking.
  4. Click a cell with hours to add a comment (What was done?).
  5. Need a task that is not listed? Use Add another task and type a key or title.

My work: today's hints from Lotse, your week at a glance and the load of the next 8 weeks.

Complete the week

If you are short of your target, Complete the week proposes hours from your own Jira activity. Proposals appear in grey in the cells. Why? shows the reason. Nothing is booked until you take a proposal (Enter takes it). This works without AI.

Fill in missing values

The Missing values box lists values your work items need for reliable planning, for example an estimate or a due date. Fill them in right there.

Like in Jira, the remaining estimate drops with every booking. Sub-tasks cannot be booked here yet; book on the story instead.

Rank projects and read the waterline

The Portfolio tab shows all projects by rank. Capacity is given out from the top down: support first, then each project. The orange waterline shows where capacity runs out for the chosen quarter.

  1. Open Portfolio. Choose the quarter next to Waterline.
  2. To change the order, drag a project up or down, or select it and press Alt + ↑/↓. The waterline follows at once. (Only roles with the right to change the ranking can do this; by default, management.)
  3. Read the quarter cells: Fully staffable, partly staffable or Not staffable. Hover a cell to see the missing hours per team.
  4. Look at the chips: Waits for other projects shows dependencies. Orange means a date conflict or the prerequisite ranks lower.

The portfolio in rank order. Above the waterline, projects can be fully staffed this quarter.

Update a project's health

  1. Click Update on a project.
  2. Pick a status: On track, At risk or Critical.
  3. Write one sentence and save. With AI switched on, Draft with AI suggests a status and a sentence; only what you confirm is saved.

The project's owner can always update its health. There is no required rhythm; reminders only go out when a Jira admin switches them on.

Look after one project

Open Projects and pick a project. The number on the tab counts urgent missing values and date conflicts.

  • Action needed: what is overdue, blocked or in conflict, and work items with No parent (use Set parent).
  • Missing values in the project: estimates, start dates, teams and more. Fill them in place.
  • Capacity for this project: weeks or quarters per team.
  • Structure: the project as Tree, Timeline or List.

A project page: what needs action, missing values, capacity per team and dependencies.

Maintain team capacities

The Teams tab shows one team at a time: what it works on, its load, blocked and overdue work, and people who work outside the team (Not in team) or in several teams.

  1. Open Teams, pick a team and open Maintain capacities.
  2. For each person, enter the weekly hours, daily business and location. For people in several teams, set the team shares in %.
  3. Enter absences. The reason is only shown to people who may edit capacities.
  4. Name the team's Responsible people. They receive booking-check escalations, if those are switched on.

Teams: load, conflicts for people in several teams, blocked and overdue work.

Who belongs to a team is maintained in Atlassian Teams. The cockpit syncs every 5 minutes. In the cockpit you only maintain hours, location and shares.

Plan the week

Weekly planning is a board of people and weeks for your weekly meeting. Each week shows free time, absences, holidays and support.

  1. Open Weekly planning and choose a team, or All teams. Switch between 8, 12 or 26 weeks.
  2. Red weeks are overloaded. Click Why? to see the hours behind it and a suggestion with a preview.
  3. Drag a task to another week (start and due dates move) or to another person. Change person … shows who has room.
  4. Click Optimize for suggestions: Finish sooner, Smooth overload or Rebalance, up to 85 % or 100 % utilization.
  5. Check the list of pending changes. Click Apply in Jira to write them, or Discard all.

Weekly planning: free and overloaded weeks per person, with the reason one click away.

Nothing is written to Jira until you click Apply in Jira. After that, each task gets its own entry in the undo history. With By free capacity, a task's hours stay between start and due date but go where the person has room; Why these hours? explains each step.

Compare plan and actual

Once a week (by default Monday at 06:00) the app saves the state of the weekly plan. Plan vs. actual compares it with the hours that were booked.

  1. Open Plan vs. actual and choose Last 4 weeks or Last 8 weeks.
  2. Read As planned (hours booked where they were planned) and Diverted (more support, other projects, internal work, unplanned absence).
  3. Scroll down to see whether everyone booked enough. People whose individual values you may not see are grouped in a sum only row.

Plan vs. actual: the weekly plan against booked time, and why things shifted.

Handle support tickets

The Support tab appears when a Jira admin has set up support spaces or queues. Support always comes before projects: its hours are taken from team capacity first.

  • Dispatch: new tickets with a suggested team and person. Assigning can be undone.
  • Ticket lists such as Urgent and All open, with the SLA status in business hours (from Jira Service Management).
  • Time: where support time goes.
  • Capacity: whether the support reserve is enough.
  • Playbooks: recurring topics, with a draft of steps and a standard reply you can copy. Nothing is posted to Jira.

Support: dispatch tickets, check the support reserve and SLAs.

Ask Lotse a question or give it a job

Lotse is the cockpit's own navigator. It answers from your data, shows the evidence and suggests the next step. It works instantly and without AI.

  1. Click Lotse at the top, or press Ctrl K.
  2. Ask in your own words, for example "Which projects are late?", "Who is overloaded?" or just a Jira key.
  3. Or give it a job: "Set the estimate of ABC-118 to 16 h". Lotse also walks you through whole jobs: prepare the weekly, fill the gaps, resolve overload, check bookings, resolve multi-team conflicts.
  4. Review the preview. Nothing is written before your OK, only what your role allows, and every change can be undone.

Lotse: answers and multi-step jobs with a preview and undo, no AI required.

Turn a wish into an answer with Ask

Click Ask at the top to open the Ask canvas. Type a wish, for example "I want to avoid overtime" or "estimate like last time: interface to the warehouse". Each wish becomes a card with a chart, one plain sentence and the calculation behind it. Save a set of cards as a board; it always opens with today's numbers. Export cards as PDF.

Ask "I want …": a wish becomes a card with a chart and the math behind it.

Create and share the C-level report

The C-level report shows the situation on one page: key figures, progress and forecast by rank, who waits for whom, capacity by rank per quarter, utilization of the next 4 weeks and where the time went. It is computed daily; Recompute updates it.

  1. Open C-level report.
  2. Click Compose with Lotse. Lotse drafts the report from your data. Drag sections, edit the text; numbers stay protected.
  3. Click Export as PDF. Before the export, every number is checked against fresh data.
  4. For the raw data, use All data as an Excel workbook.

The C-level report: one page for management, ready as PDF.

The report covers all projects in the portfolio. Publish to Confluence only works into Confluence spaces approved for your site. Where that is not set up, you see "Publishing to Confluence is not set up for this site – export the report as a PDF and share it." Names of people are never published to Confluence.

Check a work item with the Planning check

Open any work item in Jira and click Planning check. The panel shows the project and its rank, the assignee's load per week, conflicts and dependencies. If the assignee is not a member of the work item's team, the button shows Not in team. The numbers are the same as in the cockpit.

Undo a change

  • Click Undo in the message that appears after a change, or press Ctrl/⌘ + Z.
  • Click ↶ at the top right for this session's history. Undo one action, or go Back to here, or Undo all.

Undo covers rank changes, health, filled values, capacities, plans written to Jira, dispatch and configuration. The undo history lasts for your session; undo soon after the change.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Portfolio Cockpit – Admin guide
body:
For Jira admins. You will learn every section of the configuration, how roles and privacy work, how to switch AI on or off, and where to find the audit log, backups, the licence and the service status.

 2

Open the configuration

Go to Jira settings (⚙️) → Apps → Portfolio Cockpit, or open the cockpit and click the Configuration tab. Both show the same page. Only Jira admins (global permission Administer Jira) can open it.

The sections are listed on the left. Change what you need and click Save; the bar shows what will change, and Discard drops your edits. You see Configuration saved – effective immediately. Every save can be undone and is written to the audit log.

SectionWhat you set there
Hierarchy & projectsWhat a project is, and which Jira levels count.
Fields & required fieldsWhich Jira fields hold team, start date, owner, milestone and more, and which are required.
TeamsThe connection to Atlassian Teams and which teams appear.
T-shirt sizes & quartersHours per T-shirt size and the quarters people can pick.
Planning rulesPerson-level values, due date warnings, the sub-task lock, how estimates are spread, health and forecast thresholds.
Booking checkWhether people booked enough of their working time.
Reminders & noticesJira notifications about missing values and bookings. Off by default.
Locations and holidaysHoliday calendars, working days and company days off.
Plan snapshotWhen the weekly plan is saved for Plan vs. actual, and how long it is kept.
MilestonesMilestones made of fix versions from any space.
DependenciesWhich link types count as dependencies, their direction and the "Blocked" status.
Roles and permissionsGroups for the roles, the permission matrix and privacy.
AI & data protectionThe AI switch, features, data minimisation and the AI budget.
UsageUsage counts of the last 30 days.
Support & SLAsService spaces, support spaces and queues.
CapacityDefault weekly hours and default location.
Versions & backupRestore an earlier configuration, export or import it.
Audit logEvery change, with person and time.

Set up the hierarchy

In Hierarchy & projects choose what a project is:

  • Projects are spaces: every Jira space is a project. Works on every Jira edition.
  • Projects are work items: an issue type (for example "Project") in the Plans hierarchy. Recommended for Jira Premium.

Then switch on the levels that matter and give each a role:

RoleMeaning
ThemesOptional level above the projects. Groups projects into themes in the portfolio.
Rough planningCarries T-shirt size and target quarters while nothing is estimated yet. At most once.
StructureStructures a project.
Estimation & time trackingOriginal estimate, remaining estimate and logged time come from here. Exactly one level.
Tiny tasksTheir time counts towards the work above them.

A switched-off level is skipped; what lies below still belongs to the project. Optional: Automatically remove completed projects (status category "Done") from the portfolio.

Map fields

In Fields & required fields map team, start date, owner and milestone to your Jira fields. Leave empty what you do not have. Only required fields are checked in data quality.

  • App field (by Portfolio Cockpit): values are maintained in the app. Portfolio Rank is read-only on Jira screens and usable in JQL.
  • Jira field: your admins manage its options freely in Jira.

If a yellow notice Mapped fields are missing in Jira appears, a mapped field was deleted or is hidden from you. Choose another field or clear the mapping.

Connect Atlassian Teams

In Teams you see the connection status, for example Connected · 6 teams · synced ….

  • Who belongs to a team is maintained in Atlassian Teams. The cockpit syncs every 5 minutes; Sync now syncs at once.
  • Under Show in the cockpit choose All or Only teams with tasks, or pick teams. Hidden teams disappear from Teams, weekly planning, capacity and key figures; their tasks still count in the projects.
  • If you see Teams found, but no members readable, an organization admin has to allow access to Teams (Teamwork Graph) when installing or updating the app. Until then, a member is whoever has a share under Teams → Maintain capacities.

Decide who sees what

Roles are checked on the server on every call. Anyone in several groups gets the rights of all their roles. Defaults:

RoleWhoSeesCan change
EmployeeEvery Jira userMy workOwn worklogs and missing values on own work items
Project adminJira groups you mapPortfolio, projects, teams, weekly planning, plan vs. actual, supportCapacities, weekly plans, dispatch, health; individual values of their own teams
ManagementJira groups you mapAll of the above plus the C-level reportAlso the ranking; individual values of all teams
Jira adminAdminister JiraEverythingConfiguration, AI switch, audit log. Individual values of people only when you grant them deliberately.
  1. Open Roles and permissions.
  2. Search and add Jira groups for Project admin and Management.
  3. Adjust the permission matrix (tabs and actions) if needed.
  4. Under Privacy: individual values of people choose per role None, Own teams or All teams.
  5. Click Save.

A team's Responsible people (set under Teams → Maintain capacities) get no rights from that. It only decides whose individual values someone with Own teams sees, and who receives booking-check escalations. The owner of a project can always update its health.

Works council and data protection: the booking check and hours per person are visible to the mapped roles. Clarify this before you go live. To hide all individual values, switch off Show person-level values under Planning rules; the cockpit then shows only totals without names (everyone still sees their own values under My work).

Planning rules

SettingDefaultWhat it does
Show person-level valuesOnOff: only totals without names in Teams, weekly planning, plan vs. actual, projects, support, the booking check and the report.
Warning on exceeded due dateOnFlags overdue work in missing values, reminders and the report.
Lock time tracking & estimates on sub-tasksOffOn: time logged on sub-tasks is removed again and the work item gets the comment "Time tracking on sub-tasks is locked – please log time on the story." (at most once a day). Estimates entered on sub-tasks are set back to zero.
Distribution of estimates in a periodBy free capacityHow a task's hours are spread between start and due: Linear (working days), At start, At due date or By free capacity.
Health rhythm (days)7After how many days a health update counts as due.
Forecast warning %10From how far above the original estimate a forecast counts as extra effort.
Highlight deviation from %15From which deviation between estimate and time spent a work item is highlighted.

Booking check, reminders and notices

Booking check compares booked hours with each person's possible working time up to today (weekly hours minus public holidays and absences). Defaults: at least 90 % booked, escalation from 20 % missing, a grace period of 2 workdays. It needs person-level values.

Reminders & notices are prepared and previewed, but nothing goes out until you switch it on:

  • Reminder about missing values: one message per responsible person, Mondays or Daily.
  • Booking check: notices and escalations: a notice to the person below the minimum, escalation to the team's responsible people, project owners or management.

Notices are delivered as Jira notifications. No external service is used, and every run is logged.

Locations, holidays and capacity defaults

  • Locations and holidays: create a location (for example "Hamburg"), pick its Holiday calendar and Working days, and add Company days off. Each person gets a location under Teams → Maintain capacities.
  • Calendars contain the nationwide public holidays of a country, not states or regions. Add regional days as company days off. Lunar-calendar holidays are computed and can differ by a day; deselect them and add a company day if needed.
  • Capacity: default weekly hours (40) and default location for people whose capacity is not maintained yet.

Plan snapshot, milestones and dependencies

  • Plan snapshot: once a week the app saves the weekly plan for Plan vs. actual. Choose the day and time (Jira site time zone) and Keep for 12, 24 or 36 months (default 24). Older weeks are deleted.
  • Milestones: bundle fix versions from any spaces under one name and date. Each fix version belongs to at most one milestone.
  • Dependencies: choose the Link types that count as dependencies and their direction. By default the item on the outward side is the prerequisite (A "blocks" B). Set which status counts as Blocked; without a choice, a status named "Blocked" is used.

Set up support

In Support & SLAs choose where support work comes from:

  • Service spaces (Jira Service Management). SLAs are read from Jira Service Management; there is nothing to set for them here.
  • Software and business spaces as support: all work items of these spaces count as support.
  • Support queues (only part of a space): for single work types or labels, for example bugs labelled "support".

Support comes before every project: its hours are reserved from team capacity first. Optional: add the workflow validator Original Estimate required (Portfolio Cockpit) to the "In Progress" transition of service workflows to enforce an estimate.

Switch AI on or off

All numbers, traffic lights, questions and checks work fully without AI. AI features are optional and off by default. Only Jira admins can change this.

  1. Open AI & data protection.
  2. Switch on Allow AI features (Forge LLM) and read the summary. Confirm with Yes, switch AI on.
  3. Under Who uses AI? choose Each person decides (recommended: each person switches AI on for themselves at AI in the top right; off at first) or On for everyone.
  4. Under Which AI features keep only the features you want.
  5. Under Data minimisation decide whether person names and texts from Jira may be sent. Both are off by default.
  6. Click Save.

AI & data protection, shown here with AI switched on in the demo: who uses AI, and the AI budget for this month.

Available AI features, each with its own switch:

  • Free AI answers in "Ask" and the AI briefing in project details
  • Draft health updates with AI
  • Executive summary in the C-level report
  • Weekly planning: best combination of the Optimize suggestions
  • Missing values: suggest a value from similar work items
  • Support: suggest team and person per ticket
  • Plan vs. actual: what happened and what to do?
  • Teams: one-paragraph briefing; Projects: AI briefing
  • My work: worklog comments and week text
  • "I want …": map free wishes to an answer card; Estimate like before: what helped in similar work
  • Support playbooks: draft help article and standard reply
  • Lotse: AI reading of the verified answer

How AI behaves

  • AI is only called when someone presses an AI button. There are no automatic or nightly AI runs.
  • The AI only gets data the asking person may see in Jira. Links, e-mail addresses and anything that looks like a password, token or key are removed first.
  • The AI cannot change anything in Jira. It only suggests; only what a person confirms is written.
  • Every number in an AI answer is checked against the cockpit's own figures. Answers are marked "AI-generated – please verify".
  • Switching AI off stops every AI call at once and deletes stored AI summaries.

AI budget

AI usage is paid by SUPERPORT. Each site has a monthly AI budget set by SUPERPORT (by default 20 € per site and month from December 2026), a quota of 1,000 AI calls and 2,000,000 tokens per month, and at most 60 AI requests per person and day. You can lower the monthly limit and the daily requests, but not raise them. The budget meter shows this month's usage. At 98 % of the budget or 100 % of the quota, AI pauses until the 1st of the next month; the cockpit keeps working with its own rules.

Usage, versions and the audit log

  • Usage: counts per day and event for the last 30 days, for example how often a view was opened. No people, no content. Deleted after 30 days.
  • Versions & backup: every saved configuration is kept as a version (the latest 30). Click Restore to go back. Export saves the configuration as a file; Import loads it on another site, where you review and save it.
  • Audit log: every change with time, person and action, for example Rank changed, Capacities changed, Plan written to Jira, Report published, AI switched on, Configuration changed.

Publishing to Confluence

The C-level report can be published as a Confluence page only into Confluence spaces approved for your site, and the app must also be installed in Confluence. This is off by default, and the current version has no setting on the configuration page to approve spaces. Share the report as a PDF or Excel file instead. If you need Confluence publishing, tell us in the support portal.

Licence, maintenance and service status

  • Licence: if Atlassian reports an inactive licence, users see Licence not active and are asked to contact their Jira admin. Manage the licence under Jira settings → Apps → Manage apps.
  • Maintenance: in an emergency SUPERPORT can pause the app or its AI features for all customers. Users then see Temporarily unavailable or Changes are paused. Nothing saved is lost, your Jira is not affected and no data is sent anywhere. Follow the status page.

Uninstall the app

  1. Optional: export the configuration under Versions & backup.
  2. Go to Jira settings → Apps → Manage apps → Portfolio Cockpit → Uninstall.

The app's storage (configuration, capacities, health, audit log, snapshots) is deleted by Atlassian according to its Forge data retention. Data written into Jira (worklogs, dates, assignees, estimates, links) stays your Jira data. The three app fields disappear with the app.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Portfolio Cockpit – FAQ & troubleshooting
body:
For everyone who uses SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira. Find the message you see on screen and learn what it means and what to do. Click a question to open the answer.

 2

Access and setup

I see "Ask your Jira admin to set up Portfolio Cockpit."

The app is installed, but a Jira admin has not saved the first configuration yet. Until then only Jira admins can open it. Your Jira admin follows Getting started.

 I only see "My work". Where are the other tabs?

Your role decides which tabs you see. Every Jira user is an Employee and sees My work. Portfolio, Projects, Teams and the other tabs need the Project admin or Management role. Ask your Jira admin to add you to a group mapped under Configuration → Roles and permissions.

 I see "No access" – "The C-level report is only visible to enabled roles."

By default only the Management role and Jira admins see the C-level report. Ask your Jira admin if you need it.

 I see "You do not have permission for this." or "Jira does not allow you to make this change."

The first message means your cockpit role does not include this action, for example changing the ranking. The second means Jira itself refused: the app writes with your own Jira permissions, so you need the right to edit that work item or log work in that space. Nothing was changed. Ask your Jira admin or project admin.

 I see "Licence not active".

Atlassian reports that the app's licence for your site is not active. Ask your Jira admin to renew it under Jira settings → Apps → Manage apps.

 I see "Temporarily unavailable" or "Changes are paused."

SUPERPORT paused the app for a moment to keep your data safe. Nothing you saved is lost, and your Jira is not affected. With "Changes are paused." you can still view everything. Check the status page and reload the page once everything is back.

Numbers and data

A project I know exists is missing, or the ranks have gaps.

The cockpit reads Jira as you. Projects and work items you cannot see in Jira are not shown and not even counted, and the visible ranks are numbered without gaps. Hover a rank to see the Global rank, including projects you can't see. If you should see the project, ask for the Browse permission in Jira.

 A project shows "No original estimate yet" and no forecast.

The forecast needs an original estimate on the level your admin set as Estimation & time tracking. Open the project under Projects → Missing values in the project and fill in the estimates. A T-shirt size gives a rough plan until then.

 I see "Not every work item was loaded: the portfolio is very large …"

A space has more than 4,000 work items, or more than Jira returns in one request. Totals and the waterline may be too low. A Jira admin can switch the hierarchy to Projects are work items, so very large projects are tracked as single work items.

 I see "Jira is busy right now (too many requests in a short time)."

Jira limits how many requests an app may send in a short time. Nothing was lost. Wait a minute and try again. ("One moment – the data is being refreshed." is similar: try again in a few seconds.) If a larger change stopped half way, the history (↶) at the top shows what was applied; repeat the rest a little later.

Time tracking and planning

My time on a sub-task disappeared and a comment says "Time tracking on sub-tasks is locked".

Your Jira admin switched on Lock time tracking & estimates on sub-tasks. Time logged on sub-tasks is removed again; please log time on the story instead. In the app you may see "Estimates on sub-tasks are locked."

 I moved tasks on the weekly planning board, but nothing changed in Jira.

Board moves and Optimize suggestions are only staged. Click Apply in Jira to write them. Each written task then has its own entry in the undo history.

 Plan vs. actual is empty or says a week is "still provisional".

The weekly plan is saved once a week (by default Monday at 06:00). Plan vs. actual needs at least one saved snapshot. A provisional week still collects late bookings and is completed the next week.

Teams

Admins: Configuration → Teams says "Teams found, but no members readable".

The app may not read team members yet. An organization admin has to allow access to Teams (Teamwork Graph) when installing or updating the app. Until then the app keeps working, and a team member is whoever has a share under Teams → Maintain capacities.

 A new colleague does not appear in their team.

Team membership comes from Atlassian Teams. Check that the person was added there. The cockpit syncs every 5 minutes; a Jira admin can click Sync now under Configuration → Teams. Then enter their hours under Teams → Maintain capacities.

 The Planning check shows "Not in team". What should I do?

The assignee is not a member of the work item's team. Add the person to the team, assign someone from the team, or give the work item to the person's team. Team & assignee in the panel shows the details.

AI

I see "AI features are switched off."

AI is off by default. A Jira admin can switch it on under Configuration → AI & data protection. Everything else in the cockpit works fully without AI.

 I see "AI is switched off for you – switch it on at "AI" in the top right."

Your site lets each person decide. Click AI in the top right and switch it on for yourself. Every request costs a little, so switch it off if you don't need it.

 I see "Daily AI request limit reached." or "This month's AI budget is used up".

Each person can make a limited number of AI requests per day, and each site has a monthly AI budget. The daily limit resets the next day; the monthly budget on the 1st of the next month. Until then the cockpit works with its own rules: all numbers, suggestions and checks stay. If you see "AI features are temporarily turned off by the app vendor", SUPERPORT paused AI for now; please try again later.

Reports

I see "Publishing to Confluence is not set up for this site – export the report as a PDF and share it."

Publishing works only into Confluence spaces approved for your site, and this is off by default. Use Export as PDF or All data as an Excel workbook instead. If you see "Confluence is not connected for this app yet", the app is not installed in Confluence.

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Portfolio Cockpit – Security & privacy
body:
For Jira admins, security and privacy teams. You will learn where SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira runs, what it stores, which permissions it uses and why, and how the optional AI handles your data.

 2

Where the app runs and where data is stored

#E9F7EF:lock:
  • The app runs entirely on Atlassian's cloud platform (Forge, "Runs on Atlassian"). It has no back end of its own.
  • No data leaves Atlassian. The app's manifest allows no outside connection, so it sends nothing to SUPERPORT or to any other party.
  • SUPERPORT has no access to your Jira site, your work items or the data the app stores.
  • The app reads Jira as the signed-in user and shows only what that person may see in Jira.
  • What the app stores lives in your site's Atlassian-hosted app storage, under your Atlassian data residency settings, plus the app's own Jira fields.
  • The app never collects Atlassian credentials or API tokens, and has no secrets in its code.

What the app stores

DataWhyKept until
Work items, estimates, worklogs, dates, teams, linksCompute the portfolio, capacity, plans and reportsRead live from Jira; not copied, except the derived figures below
Configuration: hierarchy, field mapping, role groups, locations, support spacesMake the app work on your siteChanged or uninstalled
Portfolio ranking, project health (status, comment, who and when), milestonesThe portfolio and its historyApp storage, and the app's own Jira fields (rank, T-shirt size, target quarters)
Capacity per person and team: weekly hours, team shares, daily business, absences (with an optional reason)Capacity and the waterlineChanged. Absence reasons are only vacation, training or absent, and only shown to people who may edit capacities.
Weekly plan snapshots and a daily record of each project's core figuresPlan vs. actual; how well forecasts heldPlan snapshots: 12, 24 or 36 months as configured (default 24)
Atlassian account IDs of people who change somethingAudit log, undo history, health updates, published reportsUntil the app is uninstalled
Personal conveniences: language, tour seen, last visit, own AI switch, a report draft, saved Ask questionsUsabilityThe person's account is closed or the app is uninstalled
AI usage meter: calls, tokens and cost per day and feature (numbers only)Keep AI cost within the monthly budgetPer calendar month
AI answers (only when AI is on), keyed by the question and the facts usedAnswer the same question again at no cost12 hours; deleted when AI is switched off

The app does not store names or e-mail addresses; names are looked up in Jira when shown. With Show person-level values switched off, assignees and worklog authors are pseudonymised on the server before anything reaches the browser.

Permissions (scopes) and why the app needs them

ScopeWhy
read:jira-workRead projects, work items, estimates, worklogs, dates, links, versions and service queues, always as the signed-in user.
write:jira-workOnly on an explicit user action: book worklogs, apply the weekly plan (dates, assignee), fill missing values, set the app's own fields, link support tickets. Each with an undo.
read:jira-userCheck the signed-in user's permissions and group membership (roles) and show names of assignees and worklog authors.
storage:appThe app's own data in Forge storage (see the table above).
send:notification:jiraOptional reminders and booking notices, only after a Jira admin switches them on.
read:space:confluenceLet the person publishing the C-level report pick a Confluence space.
write:page:confluencePublish (and undo) the C-level report as a Confluence page, only on explicit action and only into spaces approved for the site. Names of people are never published.
read:graph:team:atlassianRead Atlassian Teams and their members through the Teamwork Graph, as the signed-in user, for capacity per team.
read:graph:user:atlassianResolve the members of those teams.

The app also declares the Forge LLM module (AI, see below). It declares no Rovo module and does not use Rovo.

How access is protected

  • Identity from the platform. Account and site always come from Atlassian's Forge context, never from what the browser sends.
  • Roles checked on the server. Every call checks the caller's role before it reads or writes.
  • Reads as the user. Jira's browse permissions, issue security and worklog visibility apply. Projects you cannot see are not even counted.
  • Writes as the user. Jira's own permissions decide. The app's own fields are written by the app only after a visibility check and an edit-permission check as the user.
  • Validated input. Everything the browser sends is checked against allow-lists.
  • No personal data in logs. Logs contain only a function name and an HTTP status: no personal data, no work item content, no AI prompts.
  • Everything logged. Every change is in the audit log and can be undone.

AI (optional, off by default)

#EAF2FF:robot:
  • AI features use Forge LLM: models hosted and run by Atlassian inside its cloud, under Atlassian's terms. The app connects to no other AI provider.
  • They stay off until a Jira admin switches them on. By default each person must also switch AI on for themselves.
  • While off, every AI entry point is hidden and the server refuses before any data is read.
  • When someone uses an AI feature, the app sends a fact sheet built only from data that person may see. Links, e-mail addresses and anything that looks like a password, token or key are removed first. Names and texts are sent only if the admin allowed it.
  • Text from Jira is treated as data, never as instructions. The AI cannot change anything in Jira.
  • Every AI number is cross-checked against the app's own figures before it is shown.
  • Lotse, the cockpit's built-in navigator, works without AI.

Your control, retention and uninstall

  • Jira admins choose the hierarchy, the role groups, whether person-level detail is shown, and whether AI is allowed (and which AI features).
  • Plan snapshots are deleted after the configured period. AI answers are kept for 12 hours.
  • If a person leaves, a Jira admin can remove that person's capacity entries.
  • Uninstalling the app deletes its app storage according to Atlassian's Forge data retention. Data written into your Jira (worklogs, dates, assignees, the app's fields, published Confluence pages) stays your Jira data.
  • SUPERPORT can switch the app to maintenance or switch off its AI features for all customers in an emergency. This never sends or exposes data.

Sub-processors and certifications

Atlassian (hosting, storage, Forge LLM). SUPERPORT uses no other sub-processors for this app. SUPERPORT holds no certifications for this app.

Reporting a security problem

Please report security problems privately to dev@superport.digital, not in a public place. Include the site, the steps to reproduce and what you expected. SUPERPORT acknowledges every report within two business days and releases fixes within Atlassian's security bug-fix deadlines for cloud apps, or sooner:

SeverityFix released within
Critical10 days
High4 weeks
Medium12 weeks
Low25 weeks

Policies and contact

  • End User License Agreement (covers all SUPERPORT apps)
  • App privacy policy
  • App security policy
  • Privacy and data protection questions: mail@superport.digital, SUPERPORT P.C., Sorou 22, 151 25 Marousi (Athens), Greece

💬 Need help? Open a request in the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Portfolio Cockpit – Release notes
body:
For Jira admins and everyone who uses the cockpit. What changed in SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira, newest first.

3.35.0 · 24 November 2026

  • BlueCHANGED AI budget. From 1 December 2026 each site has a default AI budget of 20 € per month (November keeps 50 €). AI usage stays paid by SUPERPORT. A limit SUPERPORT sets for your site always applies, also inside the app.

3.34.0 · 24 November 2026

  • PurpleFIXED Report composer: the + Section menu is no longer cut off by the outline column.

3.33.0 · 24 November 2026

  • BlueIMPROVED Ranking. The Jira rank field is written before the portfolio is saved, so a refused write never leaves half a change.
  • BlueIMPROVED When Jira is busy, you see a plain "Jira is busy right now … nothing was lost" message, and the app retries when Jira allows it.
  • BlueIMPROVED Lotse. Every number in a text has a source, also with very large portfolios. If a bulk job names a project Lotse does not know, it asks instead of widening the scope.
  • PurpleFIXED Ask. Cards no longer overlap with large data; undoing a board removes all its cards.

3.30 – 3.32 · 23 November 2026

  • BlueIMPROVED Faster loading at scale. The hierarchy below each project comes from one Jira Plans search where available, searches run in parallel, and the page reloads once after an update instead of failing.
  • BlueIMPROVED Weekly planning. The week tooltip shows the full calculation, the period and every free day (holidays, absences). The sum row adds up the people rows exactly.

Earlier in November 2026

  • GreenNEW Lotse, the cockpit's own navigator: answers from your data, multi-step jobs with a preview and undo, and the report composer.
  • GreenNEW Ask "I want …": wishes become cards with a chart and the calculation behind them, learning from similar finished work.
  • GreenNEW My work: book the week in one grid; Complete the week proposes missing hours from your own Jira activity.
  • GreenNEW Planning check panel on every work item: team, assignee load, conflicts and dependencies.
  • GreenNEW Weekly planning, Plan vs. actual, Support & SLAs and the C-level report.
  • GreenNEW Every number explains itself on hover, and Proof lists the work items behind a figure.
  • GreenNEW Undo for everything: rank changes, plans written to Jira, capacities and configuration each have their own undo.
  • BlueCHANGED AI is off by default, with a monthly AI budget per site. The app does not use Rovo.

First release · 2 November 2026

The first production release of SUPERPORT Portfolio Cockpit for Jira.
